states.name: library
states.gap: A's row separators are set to nothing: all seven start at x=50 CSS px — 13.5px past the document icon's right edge (36.5) and 4.5px short of the name column (54.5) — so every hairline floats between two columns instead of bracketing one. A also runs three line values where one would do: 2 CSS px #DFDFDF under the toolbar, 1px #DFDFDF at the pane edge, 1px #E2E2E2 between rows. B uses a single 1px #E7E7E7 for all three and lands each rule's left edge on the name box (rule 46, name 47).
states.gapTheirs: B's toolbar gutter is on three different left edges in three stacked items: 'Sort by Date' at 14.3 CSS px, the sidebar toggle at 15.8, the search magnifier at 19.8 — a 5.5px zigzag at the first thing you look at, where A holds the magnifier and the sort row on the same 11px line. Compounding it, B's row rules stop at 352.5px (flush with the date column) while the selected row's tint bleeds full-width to 367, leaving a 14px unruled notch wherever a rule meets the divider.
states.verdict: These are the same pane built twice; the difference is who held the ruler where. B is tidier in the list body — one hairline value, every rule's left edge on the name column, a strict 16px indent ladder — then throws it away at the top, where the search magnifier sits 5.5px right of the sort row beneath it and the toggle beneath that, and at the seam, where the rules stop 14px short of a divider the row tint runs straight into. A's faults are duller and more forgivable: hairlines that begin at 50px and align to nothing, and three line weights doing one line's job. But A's pane is the same #F7F7F7 as the page, so the library reads as a margin of the sheet rather than a panel bolted to it, and its excerpts sit 10 levels darker — and the excerpt is what you actually scan when six filenames all look like hyphenated nouns. Neither is finished; A gets out of the way faster.
